title: Albert system versus Boehm clarinet and tone
summary: New Orleans clarinetists stuck with the Albert system; he used Boehm in the Army and thinks tone comes from the player.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Do you remember any of the other clarinetists, how they held their instrument, if anybody else did that, that you ever from New Orleans had?

No, I don't remember anybody else that was more or less playing in an unorthodox style. Most of them? Most of them followed the same pattern. Yeah. And the only thing that I have found with the clarinet players in New Orleans is that they never seem to get away from the old Albert system. You find three-fourths of them a day still playing the Albert system. Yeah, Simeon and I.

Yeah. Johnny Donnells. Bonnie Bigard, Johnny Donnells, the same thing. And yet still the BAM system is supposed to be the, well, which is a developed system, and you have several ways of making a passage of notes, more so than you had with the.

It's a little easier for trills and a lot of fast work you can do better on it. I guess it's better in tune. Yes, that's right. But did you ever think, did you ever try the BAM? Did you play the BAM much?
Yes, I played the BAM in the Army at the time.
Did you still use Albert though?
Yes, I had used the BAM quite a bit. After some of the fellas had told me about it and I had the occasion to use it, I find it very helpful. Yeah, it's easier.
You didn't have to stretch as far either.
That's right. But what about the tone?
Do you think there's any difference? Does the Albert have a bigger tone or more? Well I don't think so.

I don't think, I don't look at, I think the tone qualities come from the person himself. And it was a good sound instrument and you've got a pretty good tone, but I think the tone is developed more or less by yourself.

I think so. And some instruments, I would say this, it has a flatter tone and some has a sharper tone. I mean you could detect a difference if you play a type of instrument and you are satisfied with the type of tone that you get. Of course most musicians with a good tone is never satisfied. They are always striving to get the ultimate, which we never seem to regain. But yet and still we know what we want, but we can't seem to get it, but yet and still it's pleasing to somebody else. You see what I mean? It's pleasing to somebody else, but yet and still we strive for that perfection, we strive for that perfection, but we never seem to get what we want. But yet I notice in some instruments the tone qualities are sharp in one particular instrument and sometimes it's flat in another particular instrument. Of course my instrument I had, it was a long time before I could detect anything because to begin with I had a crack in the horn I didn't even know I had. You see? And it got an instrument at such a very cheap price I was just too glad to get it. But it wasn't.
